newsitem.title: UK: LICHT SEES FALL IN EUROPEAN 97/98 SUGAR OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: LICHT SEES FALL IN EUROPEAN 97/98 SUGAR OUTPUT.

text.p: German statistician F.O. Licht on Thursday forecast an overall decline in European sugar output in 1997/98 (Sept/Aug).

European Union (EU) output was estimated to rise 18.51 million tonnes raw value from 17.98 million the previous year, while east Europe production was seen falling to 8.68 million tonnes from 9.67 million.
Overall, sugar production in Europe was forecast at 29.91 million tonnes after a previous 30.34 million.
In western Europe, Licht said excellent weather might lead to a record crop in in top grower France, where output was forecast at 4.84 million tonnes versus 4.57 million last year.
But in eastern Europe, output in Poland was expected to fall sharply from last year's 2.50 million after the recent floods. Area had also been reduced.
Turkey would be become an exporter again this year, with the industry planning to export 200,000 tonnes of white sugar in 1997, Licht said.
